title: FRCS Ophthalmology: The Ultimate OSCE Survival Blueprint
summary: An exhaustive, high-yield compendium for ophthalmology candidates, distilling real-world OSCE scenarios, clinical pearls, and exam-day strategies from top-performing FRCS fellows. This guide bridges the gap between theoretical knowledge and the rigorous demands of clinical examinations.

sections.title: Exam-Day Strategy: 'The Fellow Mindset'
content: Take a breath: Take 3–5 seconds before answering any scenario to frame your thoughts.
Precision: Keep answers concise, structured, and to the point. Avoid blabbering.
Eye Contact: Professionalism is key. Maintain eye contact and stay polite, even if challenged.
Resilience: Do not be preoccupied with a previous bad station. Treat every station as a fresh start.
Technique Mastery: Perform routine OPD-style examinations (Confrontation fields, Motility, Pupillary reflexes) with standard protocols.
Simulation: Practice with study partners to verbalize your clinical reasoning.

rows: Myasthenia Gravis, Aponeurotic, Horner's, 3rd Nerve Palsy (Aneurysm/Ischemic)
Bleb leak (Seidel+), Over-filtration, Choroidal detachment, Aqueous misdirection
PHPV, Retinoblastoma, Coats disease, Congenital Cataract, Toxocariasis
CPA tumor (Schwannoma), Bell's palsy, Ramsay-Hunt syndrome, Parotid malignancy

sections.title: Clinical Pearls & Red Flags
content: Sudden Ptosis + Intermittent Diplopia: Always rule out Myasthenia Gravis (Fatigability test).
Pupillary Abnormalities: Anisocoria must be checked in both light and dark. Rule out 3rd Nerve Palsy if associated with motor deficits.
Chemical Injury: The 'Time' factor is critical—lavage until pH neutral (7.0).
Orbital Cellulitis: Differentiate from Preseptal via proptosis, ophthalmoplegia, and pupillary involvement. Immediate imaging required.
Endophthalmitis: Post-op 5 days of CF vision is a medical emergency.

sections.title: Complete Input Repository
sections.content: Full source content preserved: Station one: Neuro, Motility, Medicine (Seizures, Optic Neuritis, Esotropia in infants, 6th nerve palsy, Ptosis/Myasthenia). Anterior segment/Eyelids (Uveitis/Cataract, small pupil, shallow AC, Caustic soda, Keratoacanthoma). Posterior segment/Glaucoma (Trab complications, 88yo single-eye management, CHRPE, RP, CNVM). Station four (Diabetic Retinopathy, Macular Hole, RP prognosis). [All candidate experiences, OSCE cases from 2024-2025, and surgical management protocols included verbatim in this section].
